collection.description: It runs from wrist almost to elbow, crooked, like a river on a map.

ask.text:
(young) has always wondered about the long, pale scar on (subject)'s forearm. It runs from wrist almost to elbow, crooked, like a river on a map.
Tonight, by the fire, (subject.he/she) finally asks.
Usually (subject) changes the subject. Usually (subject.he/she) makes a joke about wrestling a shark, or says "Oh, that old thing," and starts talking about the weather.
This time, (subject) goes quiet. (subject.He/She) turns (subject.his/her) arm over in the firelight, looking at the scar as if seeing it for the first time in years. (young) wonders if (subject.he/she) should have asked at all. Should (subject.he/she) let (subject) decide how much to share, or find somewhere quieter to talk?

choices.label: Let the Elder Decide What to Share

c1o1.text: (subject) chooses to tell only part of the story: there was a fall, a long time ago, and someone (subject.he/she) loved was there, and it was a very bad day. Nothing more. (young) doesn't ask for more, and that is respected. (subject) squeezes (subject.his/her) hand before going to bed.

c1o2.text: "No," (subject) says slowly. "I think I'd like to tell someone." (subject.He/She) asks (young) to sit close, and tells the whole story, quietly, for the first time in decades. (subject.His/Her) relatives, who thought (subject.he/she) would never speak of it, listen from the shadows with tears in their eyes.

c1.text: (young) says, "You don't have to tell me," and means it. (subject) looks up at (subject.him/her)...

c2o1.text: (subject) teaches (young) exactly how (subject.he/she) set and bound (subject.his/her) own arm that day: how to pull it straight, how to splint it with two flat sticks, how tight to wrap it, and what to watch for afterwards. It is a useful skill the youngster will not forget, and (subject.he/she) goes to share it with the healers the very next morning.

c2o2.text: (subject) starts to tell it, then falters. (subject.He/She) can't remember every detail of that day anymore. Was it raining? Who found (subject.him/her)? (subject.He/She) asks (subject.his/her) oldest friends to help fill in the gaps. They argue about the rain, but they all remember who found (subject.him/her), and the story comes back together.

c2.text: (subject) traces the scar with one finger. "I broke it. Badly. And there was nobody to help, so I had to set it myself..."

c3o1.text: By the lagoon, with only the frogs to hear, (subject) talks comfortably about the scar and the day (subject.he/she) got it, and a lot of other things besides. It turns into one of the longest conversations (young) has ever had with (subject.him/her), and the two of them are friends from then on.

c3o2.text: On the walk to the lagoon, (subject) slows, and stops. (subject.He/She) decides (subject.he/she) is too tired to go into it today, and asks to rest instead. (young) walks (subject.him/her) home. "Another time," (subject) promises at the door, and somehow (young) believes (subject.him/her).

c3.text: (young) suggests they go somewhere quieter, away from the fire and all the listening ears...
